title: Your intestines replace their inner lining every four to five days
body: The inner surface of your intestines is a single layer of cells exposed to digestive juices, food and trillions of microbes, and it wears out quickly. Stem cells tucked into tiny pits called crypts divide constantly, and their offspring mature as they migrate toward the surface, where they are shed. The whole lining is renewed roughly every four to five days, while the total number of cells stays constant, making it one of the fastest-renewing tissues in the body.
